title: Insteon device profile
description: What one Insteon product is and can do, keyed by the category and subcategory it reports.

model.description: The model number printed on the product, such as 2477D.

aliases.description: Other names the product is known by, such as earlier or marketing names and HouseLinc's name.

description.description: What the product is, in a sentence or two.

identities.description: The category, subcategory and, where they differ, firmware versions the product reports in its ID request reply.

engines.description: Which Insteon engine the product runs under each identity and firmware version, where a source states it. A version no entry covers runs an engine the catalog doesn't know.

commandSets.description: Which command set the product uses under each identity and firmware version, where a source states it. Command sets are published beside the profiles, and describe the operating flags and extended settings the product shares with others.

radio.description: How the product communicates: powerline, RF, or both. Omitted when no source states it.

role.description: Whether the product can be an ALL-Link controller, a responder, or both. Omitted when no source states it.

batteryPowered.description: Whether the product runs on batteries and sleeps between messages.

capabilities.description: What the product can do. Each kind appears at most once.

lifecycle.description: How to install the product, link it, wake it, reset it and remove it, for apps that guide people or do the steps themselves. Links are written between a controller and a responder: the device that goes into linking mode first is the controller.

installation.description: Installing the product, such as wiring a switch or plugging in a module.

linking.description: Putting the device in linking mode, as a controller or a responder.

linkingTimeoutSeconds.description: How long the device stays in linking mode if nothing links.

multiLinking.description: Linking several devices in one session.

unlinking.description: Putting the device in unlinking mode.

waking.description: Waking a battery-powered device so it can be programmed.

awakeSeconds.description: How long a woken device stays awake.

removal.description: Taking the product out of service, such as unlinking it everywhere and uninstalling it.

notes.description: Behavior worth knowing that no capability describes.

sources.description: The documents the values come from.

byte.description: A byte, written as 0x followed by two uppercase hexadecimal digits.

productKey.description: The Insteon Product Key the product reports in D2 to D4 of the Product Data Response that answers Product Data Request (cmd1 0x03, cmd2 0x00): 0x and six uppercase hexadecimal digits, D2 first. none means the product reports no key: Insteon's documents mark it Legacy, made before product keys, and such a product doesn't answer Product Data Request. Omitted when no source gives it. The identity's verification covers it too.

firmware.description: The firmware versions this identity covers, inclusive. Omitted, it covers every version.

region.description: Where the variant was sold, when the subcategory tells regions apart.

type.description: The group type, in every command set the profile's identities use, that says what the group is.

activeWhen.description: The operating flag state the group is in use under, such as a keypad's detached load (group 9), in use only while detachedLoad is set.

linkable.description: How the group can be linked: from the device's buttons, or only by software.

oneOf.description: Turns a load on and off.
A modem: a PowerLinc Modem, USB Adapter or Hub's own modem.

linkData.description: What Data 1 to 3 hold in the ALL-Link database records the modem writes itself when it links with Start ALL-Linking, so an app writing such a record by hand writes the same bytes: controller, the records in which the modem is the controller; responder, those in which it's the responder. A byte a list leaves out isn't known.

oneOf.description: A Hub's local HTTP interface, through which its modem is driven.
The Hub Pro's own HTTP interface for adding and removing devices and updating its software.
A thermostat, with the mode values it uses in mode status reports.

modeValues.description: Which table the mode report (cmd1 0x70) uses: commandTable, the table most devices use, or tempLinc, the earlier TempLinc table. Where a profile names a command set, the command set's directMessages describe the reports, and they win where the two differ.

oneOf.description: What the product means by the commands it sends to its groups.
A periodic heartbeat to a group, for noticing a product that has gone quiet.

modemLinkDataByte.description: What one data byte of a record a modem writes holds: a fixed value, or a byte of the linked device's identity as the device reported it in ALL-Linking Completed.

name.description: A name for code to refer to, in lower camel case.

value.description: The byte the modem writes, when it's always the same.

identity.description: The linked device's category, subcategory or firmware version, when the byte holds it.

firmwareSelection.description: Firmware versions: only the versions listed, or every version except them.

only.description: The firmware versions that have the capability.

except.description: The firmware versions that don't have the capability.

engine.description: The Insteon engine a product runs under one of its identities: i1, i2, or i2CS, which rejects an extended message whose D14 checksum is wrong. A device also reports its engine in reply to a get engine version command (cmd1 0x0D).

firmware.description: The firmware versions that run the engine. Omitted, every version does.
The firmware versions that use the command set. Omitted, every version does.

verification.description: How the catalog knows the value. Omitted means documented: an Insteon document gives it and none of the catalog's sources disagree.

status.description: documented: an Insteon document gives the value, as when the field is omitted, and the note says more. inferred: no document states it; it's read from an example, a similar product or the product's behavior, as the note explains. conflicting: Insteon's documents disagree; the note says what each gives, and the value is the one the catalog uses. observed: the value has been seen on a device, running the firmware versions listed; the note says what was seen.

note.description: What the status rests on: the documents and what each says, or what was observed.

firmware.description: For observed values, the firmware versions the devices it was seen on were running.

step.description: One step a person or an app takes: what to do, to which control, for how long or how many times, and what the device does in answer.

text.description: The step as a person reads it, in the owner's manual's words where it has them.

device.description: Which device the step is done on: this one, or the other device being linked or unlinked. Defaults to this one.

action.description: What the step does, for an app that guides it or does it itself.

control.description: The button or part the step uses, as the device labels it, such as SET button.

seconds.description: How long to hold, wait or keep going, for a hold, wait or press step.

count.description: How many times to tap or press. A step that taps and then holds is two steps.

expect.description: What the device does when the step works, such as the LED blinking green or a beep.

command.description: For a step an app sends, the Insteon command, by its Developer's Guide name, such as Enter Linking Mode.

procedure.description: Steps in order, and how sure the catalog is of them.

description.description: What this way of doing it is, for an alternative, such as From software or As a responder.

alternatives.description: Other ways to do the same thing, such as from software instead of with the SET button. Each is a whole procedure; an app follows one.
